title: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy (2029)
author: Asha Patel
summary: Company-wide policy and operational playbook covering annual budgeting and rolling forecasts, procurement approval and vendor onboarding, contracts lifecycle and approval matrix, and revenue recognition & billing rules for Redwood Inference.
body:
Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference's consolidated finance and legal policies for budgeting and forecasting, procurement, contracts, and revenue recognition/billing. It is intended to provide clear procedures, approval matrices, and control checkpoints to ensure compliance, predictable financial planning, and scalable vendor/contract management across Hosted, Dedicated and Private product lines.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood business units and global entities unless a legal entity-specific policy exists.
- Covers annual budgeting, quarterly rolling forecasts, purchase and vendor commitments, contract review/approval, and revenue recognition for hosted usage, reserved capacity, enterprise licensing, and add-ons.
- Does NOT replace special regulatory or country-specific requirements (e.g., tax law, local accounting rules) which must be followed in addition to this policy.

Definitions:
- Budget: the approved annual operating plan (Opex/Capex) for a fiscal year.
- Forecast: a rolling projection of financial results (monthly/quarterly) used for liquidity and capacity planning.
- Vendor Commitment: any purchase order (PO), contract, or reservation that creates a legal or economic obligation.
- RevRec: revenue recognition policies that determine when and how revenue is recorded in the general ledger.

Roles and Ownership:
- Finance (FP&A): owns the budgeting and forecasting cadence, templates, variance analysis and consolidation.
- Legal: owns contract language standards, risk reviews, and final signatory guidance.
- Procurement (centralized function within Finance): owns vendor onboarding, PO issuance, vendor master data, and procurement controls.
- Product & GTM Leaders: provide demand/capacity assumptions, product pricing inputs, and commercial term requirements.
- Engineering / IT: provide hardware capacity forecasts and procurement requests for infra (GPU fleet, networking).

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (Annual + Rolling):
Overview:
- Annual budget cycle runs from August–November for the next fiscal year. Final budget approval occurs in December.
- Rolling forecast updated monthly; material changes (>=5% variance to key line items) must be escalated to FP&A and Exec Finance.

Process (high-level):
1. Calendar & templates published by FP&A by Aug 1.
2. Departments submit base budgets and supporting assumptions by Sep 15.
3. Finance consolidation and leadership reviews occur Oct 1–Nov 15.
4. Exec review and final approval by Board/CEO in Dec.
5. Monthly forecasting window: data lock on the 5th business day; forecast published by the 10th.

Mandatory Inputs:
- Headcount plan (by role band), hiring timeline, and average loaded cost per FTE.
- Infrastructure capacity plan (GPU-hours, reserved capacity needs).
- Revenue drivers by product (Hosted API tokens, Dedicated contracts committed throughput, Private deployment licenses).
- One-time investments (R&D projects, strategic hires, on-prem packaging).

Controls and SLOs:
- Variance reporting: monthly variance >= 5% on revenue or >= 10% on expense categories must include root cause and corrective plan.
- Budget change requests after approval require a documented business case and sign-off from the budget owner and FP&A.

2) Procurement Procedures and Vendor Commitments:
Policy Highlights:
- Procurement is required for all vendor commitments > $5,000 (contract value or incremental PO).
- Emergency purchases (unplanned, < $10k) allowed with after-the-fact procurement logging and an incident justification.

Approval Matrix (simplified):
- <= $5k: Requestor -> Department Manager.
- $5k – $50k: Requestor -> Department Manager -> Procurement.
- $50k – $250k: Requestor -> Department Manager -> Procurement -> Finance Director.
- > $250k: Requestor -> Department Manager -> Procurement -> VP Finance -> Legal -> CEO (if multi-year strategic).

Vendor Onboarding Checklist:
- Supplier questionnaire (AML/KYC, tax W-9/W-8, bank details).
- Insurance requirements (commercial general liability, cyber insurance if handling customer data).
- Data processing addendum (DPA) for vendors that process Redwood customer data.
- Payment terms & early-pay discount negotiation (default net 30).

Procurement Request Steps (numbered):
1. Open a procurement request in the Procurement portal and attach estimates and justification.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor alternatives and compliance requirements (security, privacy, sanctions).
3. Legal reviews contract template and risk sections for material services.
4. Finance confirms budget availability (budget check).
5. PO issued and supplier added to vendor master before first invoice payment.

Spend Threshold Table:
- Threshold | Required Approvals | Additional Controls
- <= $5k | Dept manager | No PO required (automated card spend allowed)
- $5k–$50k | Procurement + Dept manager | Standard PO and 2-way match
- $50k–$250k | Finance Director + Procurement | 3-way match and supplier due diligence
- > $250k | VP Finance + Legal + Procurement | Board-level review for multi-year commitments over $1M

3) Contracts & Legal Process:
Contract Lifecycle:
- Intake -> Risk Triage -> Commercial Negotiation -> Legal Review -> Signature -> Clause Library / Obligations Tracking -> Renewal/Closeout.

Minimum Legal Review Criteria:
- Any contract that: (a) contains indemnity or unusual liability caps, (b) is multi-year, (c) involves data processing, (d) exceeds $50k in expected spend or revenue.

Standard Clause Requirements (examples):
- Data protection: DPA meeting Redwood baseline (encryption, subprocessor controls, breach notification within 72 hours).
- Liability: mutual liability cap tied to the higher of (12 months fees OR $250k), subject to product-side escalation.
- IP & Models: work-for-hire vs license boundaries must be explicit for model artifacts and derivatives.
- Termination: termination for convenience (with defined exit assistance and data return), termination for cause, and transition support for Private deployments.

Approval Matrix (Contract sign-off):
- Up to $50k revenue/expense: Legal counsel + Department head.
- $50k–$250k: Legal senior counsel + Finance Director.
- > $250k or material data exposure: GC + VP Finance + CEO sign-off.

Contract Tracking & Obligations:
- All signed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (DocStore) within 48 hours with metadata: counterparty, effective date, term, renewal window, budget code, and owner.
- Contract owners must maintain an obligations register (deliverables, SLAs, data deletion timelines).

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies (RevRec):
Principles:
- Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 principles: identify contract(s) with a customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize when (or as) obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific Guidance:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as services are delivered (over time) based on measured usage in the billing period. Deferred revenue arises for prepaid credits and is amortized over the consumption period.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): For committed capacity with upfront payment, allocate revenue between capacity reservation (recognized over the reservation period) and overage usage (recognized as used).
- Private deployment (licenses + support): Distinguish license (may be recognized at a point in time if control transfers) from support and maintenance (recognized over time). Enterprise onboarding/implementation fees: assess whether they are a separate performance obligation; if not distinct, defer and recognize over the customer relationship period.
- Add-ons (observability retention, premium SLA): recognized over the term they are delivered.

Billing and Invoicing Rules:
- Standard billing cycle: net 30 after invoice date unless contractual terms specify otherwise.
- Invoices must reference contract ID, PO number (if applicable), billing period, and settlement details.
- Disputed invoices: customer must notify within 30 days; investigation period is 30 days. Adjustments made via credit memos; do not net in future invoices without documented approval.

Deferred Revenue & Cutoffs:
- Month-end cutoffs: usage data must be captured, validated and signed off by billing ops before the 3rd business day of the next month.
- Prepayments recorded as deferred revenue and amortized based on expected consumption patterns or contract terms.

Recognizing Multi-Element Arrangements:
- Use contract-level allocation to split transaction price across performance obligations. Maintain a standard mapping table in the RevRec workbook documenting typical allocations for common bundles (e.g., license + 12 months support + onboarding).

5) Controls, Auditability, and Record Retention:
- Segregation of duties: requestor, approver, and payment operator must be distinct roles for commitments > $50k.
- Audit trail: all procurement requests, contract redlines, and approvals must be retained in DocStore and procurement systems for a minimum of 7 years.
- Internal audit quarterly sampling: Finance will run transactional sampling on POs > $25k and contracts > $50k to review compliance to this policy.

6) Exceptions & Escalations:
- Small-value emergency exceptions (see Procurement Emergency) require post-facto documentation within 5 business days and a retroactive budget check.
- For legal risk exceptions (e.g., unusual IP clauses requested by strategic partner), Legal must provide a documented risk memo and mitigation plan; VP Finance and GC must approve.

Operational Checklists (quick reference):
- Budget Change Request: Business case -> Updated financials -> FP&A approval -> Exec sign-off (if > $250k incremental spend).
- Procurement Request: Request form -> Vendor due diligence -> Legal & Security review (if applicable) -> PO issuance -> Vendor onboarding.
- Contract Sign-off: Commercial terms agreed -> Legal redline -> Risk memo (if required) -> Signed & uploaded to DocStore.

- Contract repository (DocStore): https://docstore.redwood.internal/contracts

Appendix B: Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Who to contact for emergency procurement?
A: Procurement on-call (procurement@redwood.internal) and Finance Director (daniel.kim@redwood.internal).

Q: What if a vendor requests non-standard IP terms?
A: Escalate immediately to Legal; Legal will produce a risk memo and negotiate guardrails.
